questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Tanzania about 947,303 square kilometres; Botswana about 581,737 square kilometres; Burundi about 27,834 square kilometres; Monaco about 2 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Tanzania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Regions” part of the Tanzania article.

questions.proof: Tanzania's regions are: Arusha · Dar es Salaam · Dodoma · Geita · Iringa · Kagera · Katavi · Kigoma · Kilimanjaro · Lindi · Manyara · Mara · Mbeya · Morogoro · Mtwara · Mwanza · Njombe · Pemba North · Pemba South · Pwani · Rukwa · Ruvuma · Shinyanga · Simiyu · Singida · Songwe · Tabora · Tanga · Zanzibar Central/South · Zanzibar North · Zanzibar Urban/West

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Tanzania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Tanzania on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Dodoma?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Tanzania is Dodoma.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Tanzania?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Tanzania is the Tanzanian shilling.
